title: Doctor fixes you can run
summary: Every ia doctor check now carries a structured fix beside its remedy: the command as an argument vector, its flow (preview then apply, a preview flag, confirm, or immediate) derived from the command's own grammar, and what it writes; a package-manager fix names its directory explicitly, and --json gains only the fix field. Doctor adds a kits row and one kit-update row per installed kit behind, read from an update cache kept per registry, with the fix that moves each by its source (an npm package, a registry collection or a release), and a marketplace row that says when the marketplace was last checked. ia-distribution refresh-updates takes --root and --force, refreshes asynchronously and merges under the IA home's store lock. A registry collection's identity is kept beside the lock in .ia/kit-collections.json, the lock itself unchanged, and installing a collection again replaces its members. An apply refuses a .ia/kit-collections.json it cannot decode with IA-DIST-COLLECTIONS-UNREADABLE, before any write, instead of replacing it. Doctor adds a home-lock row, with no fix, for an IA home store lock whose owner on this host is gone. Extensions can contribute console areas, offers and checks as data; an extension fix takes its flow and target from the console's declared step, and one no step declares asks first and targets the machine.
